title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2605.27922v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed as executable systems that use tools, modify workspaces, and produce concrete artifacts. In such workflows, performance depends not only on the base model, but also on the harness: the system layer that manages context, tools, state, constraints, permissions, tracing, and recovery. However, existing benchmarks typically abstract away execution, compare complete agent systems, or hold the harness fixed, making execution-layer variation difficult to study. We introduce Harness-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating configuration-level harness effects in realistic agent workflows. Harness-Bench evaluates representative harness configurations across multiple model backends under shared task environments, budgets, and evaluation protocols, while preserving each harness's native execution behavior. translated_title: Harness-Bench：跨模型与真实工作流的智能体框架（Harness）评估基准

tldr: 该论文提出Harness-Bench，一个包含106个沙盒化真实任务的诊断基准，首次在多个模型后端上系统评估LLM智能体执行层框架（harness）配置对性能的影响。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Harness-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with 106 sandboxed realistic tasks that for the first time systematically evaluates configuration-level effects of LLM agent harnesses—the execution layer managing context, tools, state, and permissions—across multiple model backends.
